description: Down-migration registry. Maps up-migrations to their reverse. Used by migration-runner --down to pick the right script. Not every up has a down — gold-standard append-only invariants (audit chain, event store) require explicit dev/staging-only down-flags. See LITFIN-parity item 5.
scope: 10 highest-blast-radius migrations from 0252..0273, the 0317/0318 Borjie-parity RLS+idempotency ports, and the 0319..0323 parity-final back-port (portal-genui tabs/records/self-healing + connector-OAuth credentials/nonces). Older migrations get down scripts in follow-up passes.

mappings.reverses: CREATE TABLE connector_credentials + idx_connector_creds_tenant_kind + idx_connector_creds_expiry + FORCE RLS tenant_isolation_connector_credentials + connector_credentials_service_role_bypass + REVOKE anon
mappings.notes: Connector-OAuth completion (#12, Borjie 0343). Per-tenant per-account OAuth credential store; access/refresh token columns are AES-GCM ciphertext sealed with a tenant-bound DEK (the database NEVER sees plaintext). Tenant-isolated, FORCE RLS. Dropping forces every connector to be reconnected. MUST NOT run in production: discards every tenant's connector OAuth state.

mappings.reverses: CREATE TABLE oauth_state_nonces + oauth_state_nonces_created_idx + FORCE RLS oauth_state_nonces_tenant_isolation + oauth_state_nonces_service_role_bypass + REVOKE anon
mappings.notes: Connector-OAuth completion (#12). DURABLE single-use consumption of the connector-OAuth `state` nonce — multi-replica replay protection (a per-process Set cannot defend across replicas). Nonces are opaque random values: no PII, no token material, so the data loss is benign. Dropping re-opens cross-replica OAuth state replay until restored.

mappings.reverses: CREATE TABLE tenant_deletion_schedules + status/grace CHECKs + partial-unique active-per-tenant idx + due/tenant idx + FORCE RLS tenant_isolation + service_role_bypass + REVOKE anon
mappings.notes: R2 blocker #8 fix: durable backing for the tenant-wide right-to-erasure surface DELETE /api/v1/tenants/:id, which was a silent no-op (resolved an unwired tenantDeletion service and returned 202 without persisting). The route now writes a 'scheduled' row before returning success; the platform tenant-purge worker consumes status='scheduled' AND scheduled_purge_at <= now() at grace expiry. Dropping discards scheduled erasure requests; the surface regresses to audit-event-only until re-created.

mappings.reverses: CREATE TABLE applicant_notifications (+ tenant/applicant + unread indexes) + CREATE TABLE rfb_responses (+ tenant/rfb index + partial-unique accepted-per-request) + FORCE RLS tenant_isolation + service_role_bypass + REVOKE anon on both
mappings.notes: Mode-C R2 counterparty highs: (a) applicant_notifications backs the tenant-mobile L7 inbox (GET /api/v1/notifications -> { data: { notifications } } + POST /:id/read backed by read_at) which previously read the operator dispatch log and was permanently empty; (b) rfb_responses backs the accepted-response lookup the L8 Sign-Lease/sign-delivery settlement loads. Both tenant-scoped, FORCE RLS, applicant-scoped anti-IDOR at the route. Dropping (a) regresses the inbox to permanently-empty; dropping (b) regresses Sign-Lease to an honest no-accepted-response empty state.

mappings.reverses: DROP non-partial org_memberships_identity_org_active_idx + CREATE non-partial org_memberships_identity_org_idx (restores the pre-0339 index)
mappings.notes: Mode-C R2 identity high: 0024's org_memberships unique index over (tenant_identity_id, organization_id) was NON-partial, so re-redeeming an invite after a retained LEFT/BLOCKED row threw a unique-violation surfaced as an opaque 500 (re-join impossible). 0339 makes uniqueness PARTIAL on status='ACTIVE' so at most one live membership per (identity, org) while history coexists; schema mirror identity.schema.ts updated in lockstep. Down restores the non-partial index and will ABORT (safe) if a LEFT + ACTIVE row would now collide. Indexes only — no rows touched.

mappings.reverses: ADD COLUMN work_orders.assigned_to_user_id (TEXT REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL) + partial index work_orders_assigned_to_user_idx (tenant_id, assigned_to_user_id) WHERE assigned_to_user_id IS NOT NULL
mappings.notes: Mode-C R2 owner↔workforce HIGH: makes work_orders.assigned_to_user_id the ONE canonical worker assignee, bridging the previously-unbridged work_orders (vendor-only) vs assignments (worker-keyed) models. Stamped by POST /api/v1/manager/work-orders/:id/assign-worker (which also creates a bridge assignments row) and surfaced by /api/v1/field/staff/tasks/next. Additive ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, FORCE RLS inherited from 0155/0156 — forward-apply is prod-safe. Dropping discards recorded WO assignees; dispatch regresses to vendor-only and /tasks/next falls back to bridge assignments rows only.

mappings.reverses: Restore the 0301 admin_four_eye_role_chk (proposed_by_role IN SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN/SUPPORT, no approved_by_role floor) in place of the tightened SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN-only proposer+approver CHECK
mappings.notes: Mode-C R2 security #23: the four-eye gate on admin_superpower_pending_approvals only enforced DISTINCT actor IDs, never a ROLE floor, so two read-mostly SUPPORT operators could collude to PROPOSE+APPROVE a HIGH-risk destructive cross-tenant verb (suspend_tenant_org / force_password_reset / force_lease_termination / export_regulator_pack). 0343 tightens admin_four_eye_role_chk to SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN for proposed_by_role and (when set) approved_by_role, as the DB backstop to the route-layer requireRole(SUPER_ADMIN,ADMIN)+isAdminFloor() guards on POST /bulk-action,/approve,/reject in superpowers.hono.ts. Constraint swap only — no rows touched. Down re-admits SUPPORT at the DB level (route guards still hold); MUST NOT run in production.

mappings.reverses: DROP POLICY event_outbox_service_role_bypass on public.event_outbox (additive permissive FOR ALL bypass gated on app.is_service_role)
mappings.notes: Mode-C R2 RLS-darkness #29: the admin superpower dispatchers (bulk-action-dispatchers.ts enqueueOutbox) write a CROSS-TENANT event_outbox actuation row (tenant_id = TARGET tenant, or NULL broadcast) under the acting admin's own app.current_tenant_id GUC, so FORCE-RLS event_outbox_tenant_isolation REJECTED it for any cross-tenant target while the route journal said 'applied' (born-dark: tenant suspended with no outbox row to drain). enqueueOutbox now wraps the insert in withServiceRoleContext; 0344 adds the matching service_role_bypass policy (same shape as 0336/0337) so the WITH CHECK passes. Additive permissive policy OR-composes with tenant_isolation — ordinary tenant-scoped outbox writes/reads unchanged. Dropping re-darkens the admin four-eye side-effects but loses no data.

mappings.reverses: CREATE TABLE session_memory, skills (PK id,version), pending_threads, thread_summaries — the 4 tenant-scoped persistent-memory / skill-library tables + their indexes, CHECK constraints, FORCE-RLS tenant_isolation + service_role_bypass policies, and anon REVOKEs
mappings.notes: CORE port (uplift ratchet) of the persistent-memory subsystem from the green sibling vertical (Borjie drizzle/0030, carried in final post-0297 shape: canonical app.current_tenant_id GUC + FORCE RLS, plus a service-role-bypass policy for cross-tenant decay/TTL sweeps per the 0337 house idiom). Tables back Mr. Mwikila's temporal-continuity substrate (session_memory, skills, pending_threads, thread_summaries). No FK on tenant_id, no pgvector (these 4 carry no embedding column). Forward-apply is prod-safe (all CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, NOT NULLs on fresh columns only). Dropping discards durable memory; continuity regresses to in-memory-only until re-created.
